question.problem: The manager at a water bottle factory notices that, on average, every batch of water bottles has $7$ water bottles on which the label is upside down. What is the probability that the next batch of water bottles will have more than $2$ bottles on which the label is upside down? Round your answer to $3$ decimal places. You may assume that upside-down labels occur independently and at a constant average rate.
question.worked_solution:
A Poisson random variable $X$ with rate $\lambda $ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{\lambda }^{x}{e}^{-\lambda }}{x!}
$$

Let $X$ be the number of water bottles on which the label is upside down. Since the average rate is $7$ upside-down labels per batch, and events occur independently and at a constant average rate, the number of upside-down labels can be modeled as a Poisson random variable with rate $\lambda =7,$ and we can write $X∼\text{Po}(7).$ 

So, $X$ has the following probability mass function:

$$
f(x)=\frac{{7}^{x}{e}^{-7}}{x!}
$$

To compute $P(X>2),$ we will use the complement:

$$
P(X>2)=1-P(X\le 2)
$$

Computing the probability of the complement, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X\le 2) & =P(X\in {0,1,2}) \\  & =f(0)+f(1)+f(2) \\  & =\frac{{7}^{0}{e}^{-7}}{0!}+\frac{{7}^{1}{e}^{-7}}{1!}+\frac{{7}^{2}{e}^{-7}}{2!} \\  & ≈0.030\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.

Therefore, the probability of finding more than $2$ upside-down labels in the next batch is

$$
\begin{aligned}P(X>2) & =1-P(X\le 2) \\  & ≈1-0.030 \\  & =0.970\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to $3$ decimal places.
